bgm_001: You can recognise them by their two huge trunks and woody knees rising from the ground at the water's edge. They stand beside the small lake in Parco Marenzi.
bgm_002: You can recognise it by its flat, layered branching and thick trunk, standing beside a sequoia and a ginkgo. It stands in Parco Caprotti.
bgm_003: You can recognise it by its dark leaves carrying white flowers and red fruit together in late autumn. It stands in the park below the Rocca fortress, in Citta Alta.
bgm_005: You can recognise it by its lightning conductor, fenced root plate and drooping crown tip, standing alone on open lawn. It stands in Parco Frizzoni in Pedrengo, with three more large cedars nearby.
bgm_006: You can recognise it as the largest tree in the park, on the high bank above the Serio river, near the old Moroccan-style greenhouse. It stands in Parco Piccinelli in Seriate.
bgm_008: You can recognise it by its pollarded crown, cut back by roughly a third after an unauthorised trim. It stands along Viale delle Rimembranze, in the centre of Torre Boldone.
